acceptance: Reproduce: with an unrelated tracked edit in the primary that overlaps member scope, show which batch commands refuse and why the member's own worktree state does not matter.

Decide by evidence whether the refusal should use the primary-clone snapshot model from PR #3888 (only changes made since the batch started, or only by this batch's members), warn instead of refuse for foreign changes, or keep refusing with a precise owner diagnostic.
Whatever the choice, a batch is never blocked silently: the message names the paths and that they are not the batch's, and guidance says what to do.
Tests cover own-member stray edits (still refused) versus foreign pre-existing edits.
context: Related done item batch-primary-clone-dirty-guard-20261104 introduced the refusal. Guardrail: do not weaken detection of the batch's own stray writes (see relative-path-primary-writes-recur-after-guard-20261110). Verification rubric: reproduce; fix; tests; comment-policy and ruff; PR merged with green CI.
description: batch-member-create, batch-member-check and batch-land refuse while the primary clone has uncommitted tracked changes in member scope. During this session other sessions' edits (.github/workflows/review-gate.yml and review-verdict.yml, scripts/batch_integration.py, benchbox/platforms/base/mysql_wire.py, psycopg2_mixin.py, pg_mooncake.py) blocked two unrelated batches for up to hours, and the leader could only wait. The guard protects the primary but turns any concurrent session's slip into a stall for everyone.
